title: Infra: GPU Fleet, Cloud Networking, Terraform/IaC, and CI/CD Playbook
author: Maya Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates our operational patterns and standards for: GPU fleet & capacity management, cloud accounts and VPC/networking controls, Terraform / Infrastructure-as-Code modules, and CI/CD pipelines for infra and runtime updates. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners who run Redwood's inference infrastructure (hosted + dedicated).

Goals
- Provide prescriptive runbooks for capacity scaling and incident triage.
- Standardize Terraform module patterns and naming conventions.
- Define CI/CD pipeline stages, approvals, and rollback strategies.
- Capture networking guardrails for multi-account deployments and private clusters.

Owner and Scope
- Primary owner: infra-platform team (contact: infra-platform@redwood.ai).
- Secondary stakeholders: eng-sre, eng-serving-runtime, security.
- Applies to all cloud-hosted GPU clusters (prod, staging, dev) and any Private/VPC customer deployments where we manage IaC.

1) GPU Fleet & Capacity Management

Summary:
GPU fleet includes pooled nodepools across regions and zones. We maintain two capacity concepts: reservation capacity (dedicated pools for Reserved customers) and burst capacity (shared pools for hosted API).

SLOs & Targets:
- Node provisioning lead time: median 4 minutes (target), p95 < 10 minutes.
- Fleet utilization target: 60-75% for cost/capacity balance.
- Spare headroom for burst: 10% of total capacity per-region.

Key Metrics to Monitor:
- GPU utilization by model class (tokens/sec per-GPU).
- Job queue length / backpressure per nodepool.
- Pod scheduling latency and preemption events.
- Spot/Preemptible eviction rate (if used) and corresponding fallback activation.

Capacity Planning Procedure (weekly):
1. Run the capacity report job: infra/tools/gpu_capacity_report --window 7d --region us-west1
2. Review utilization and 14-day demand trend.
3. If projected shortfall > 8% in any region, open a capacity change ticket in JIRA with proposed nodecounts and CIDR impact.
4. Schedule nodepool resize during maintenance window (see CI/CD steps for deployment schedule).

Autoscaling Rules (implemented in cluster-autoscaler and custom controllers):
- Scale-up: add a nodepool when average pending pods > 5 for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Scale-down: remove nodes when node utilization < 10% for 30 minutes and pods can be scheduled elsewhere.
- Reservation pools respect affinity: dedicated reservations cannot be preempted for hosted workloads.

Handling Spot Evictions:
- Eviction event -> Prometheus alert GPU_SPOT_EVICTION_HIGH -> SRE runbook: restart affected replicas on non-spot pool and notify capacity on-call.

2) Cloud Accounts & Networking

Account Topology:
- Per-environment accounts: production, staging, dev.
- Per-customer dedicated accounts for Private customers (where we manage infra) with VPC peering or PrivateLink.
- Central infra account for shared services (logging, metrics, CI runners).

VPC & Subnet Standards:
- VPC per-account. Use RFC1918 addressing with the following reserved blocks: prod: 10.0.0.0/16, staging: 10.1.0.0/16, dev: 10.2.0.0/16.
- Subnet segmentation: control-plane subnets (no external egress), workload subnets (restricted egress), public-ingress subnets.

Networking Guardrails:
- All egress to the public internet must go through NAT gateways with egress logging enabled.
- IAM + Security Group rules must follow least privilege; default deny inbound.
- PrivateLink/Peering: use VPC-Peering for intra-cloud internal services, PrivateLink for cross-account (customer) access to hosted control plane.

DNS and Service Discovery:
- Internal DNS zones: redwood.internal. Use Route53/Cloud DNS private zones per-account and replicate records using automation.

Firewall/ACL Checklist (pre-deployment):
- Verify no 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rules on workload subnets.
- Confirm NAT and Transit Gateway routes.
- Confirm IAM roles for node pools are constrained to necessary S3/GCS buckets and KMS keys.

3) Terraform / IaC Modules and Patterns

Module Naming and Layout:
- Modules live in infra/terraform/modules. Name modules using: <provider>_<service>_<purpose> (e.g., gcp_k8s_nodepool_gpu).
- Root stacks per-environment: infra/terraform/stacks/{prod,staging,dev}/{core,clusters,services}.

Module Contracts:
- Every module must include: inputs.md, outputs.md, examples/ minimal usage, and a CHANGELOG.md.
- Inputs must have clear defaults and type annotations. Optional inputs must be nullable.

State Management and Backups:
- Remote state in centrally managed backend (GCS bucket with KMS encryption). State file naming: redwood-terraform-{env}-{stack}.tfstate.
- Enable state locking (Terraform Cloud or backend locks).

Acceptance Criteria for Module PRs:
- Terraform fmt/tflint policy pass.
- Unit test via terraform-compliance or kitchen-terraform where applicable.
- Integration preview: plan applied to a throwaway environment (dev-temp) and smoke-tested.
- Peer review by at least one infra owner + security reviewer for IAM/KMS changes.

Example: gcp_k8s_nodepool_gpu inputs snippet (as example)
```
variable "node_count" { type = number default = 2 }
variable "machine_type" { type = string default = "n1-standard-16" }
variable "accelerator_type" { type = string default = "nvidia-tesla-a100" }
variable "accelerator_count" { type = number default = 1 }
```

4) CI/CD and Build Pipelines for Infra

Pipeline Stages (preferred):
1. Lint & Static Analysis (terraform fmt, tflint, terragrunt-hclfmt).
2. Unit Tests (kitchen-terraform or terraform-compliance).
3. Plan (run terraform plan with plan artifact).
4. Approval gate (manual for prod with SRE and Security).
5. Apply (automated for non-prod; scheduled for prod during maintenance windows).
6. Post-deploy smoke tests and telemetry checks.

Naming & Branching:
- Branch: feature/<short-desc> or hotfix/<desc>.
- PR title must reference related JIRA ticket. Include a short summary and risk assessment.

Apply Strategy and Rollbacks:
- Non-prod: auto-apply after CI passes.
- Prod: require at least one infra owner + security approver; applies only during the maintenance window assigned.
- Rollback: Revert PR and apply the previous stable plan (recorded in pipeline artifacts). In emergencies, apply a targeted patch to restore service and then follow a postmortem.

Secrets and Keys:
- CI secrets stored in Vault/Secret Manager with short TTL. No long-lived keys in pipeline.
- KMS keys rotated annually; rotation schedule tracked in infra calendar.

CI Runner Topology:
- Use central self-hosted runners in infra account with access to remote state. Runners tagged and isolated by environment (prod runners restricted).

5) Runbooks (Ops + Incident)

Common On-call Playbook (short):
1. Triage: identify impacted regions/clusters via dashboards (Grafana, Kibana).
2. Scope: determine whether issue is capacity, networking, control-plane, or model-serving.
3. Mitigate: scale up GPU nodes from non-prod nodepool, promote warm nodes, or divert traffic to other regions.
4. Communicate: trigger incident bridge, update status.redwood.ai, notify affected customers.
5. Postmortem: create incident ticket and assign action items within 72 hours.

Example Incident: Excessive scheduling latency (symptoms: pending pods, high scheduler latency)
- Verify scheduler logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs deployment/kube-scheduler --since=1h
- Check api-server latency and etcd: kubectl get --raw=\"/metrics\" | grep apiserver_request_latencies
- If API server is overloaded: scale control-plane (if self-managed) or raise ticket with cloud provider for managed control plane.
- Temporary mitigation: cordon low-priority nodes, increase replicas with nodeSelector to warmer pools.

Routine Playbooks:
- Monthly: run terraform plan for all stacks and reconcile drift.
- Quarterly: capacity forecast and archive unused nodepool images.
- Annual: KMS key rotation and IAM role review.

6) Operational Checklist for Releases
- Verify terraform fmt and tflint pass.
- Confirm plan artifact and reviewer sign-off.
- Confirm maintenance window and ops pager on-call present.
- Smoke test endpoints: metrics ingestion, model inference sample, control-plane API.

7) Documentation & Knowledge Sharing (infra team wiki rules)
- Keep module READMEs up-to-date; include example usage and cost implications.
- Runbook updates must be submitted as PRs to this repo; reviewers include on-call and SRE.
- Maintain a changelog for infra changes; large changes require a short design doc (ADR) linked in PR.

Appendix: Useful Commands & Shortcuts
- Capacity report: infra/tools/gpu_capacity_report --region=us-west1 --window=7d
- Resize nodepool (example): gcloud container node-pools update gpu-pool --cluster=redwood-prod --num-nodes=10 --zone=us-west1-a
- Terraform plan for stack: terragrunt plan --terragrunt-working-dir infra/terraform/stacks/prod/clusters
- Lock state: gsutil acl ch -u infra-service-account@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com:W gs://redwood-terraform-prod
